name: Melasma
statement: Melasma is a distinct, hormonally influenced form of pigmentation that responds differently to standard pigment treatment.
happening: Melasma is a specific pattern of pigmentation influenced by hormonal factors and sun exposure, and it behaves differently from general sun damage, including a higher chance of recurrence and a lower tolerance for heat-based treatment. Because of this, treatment is usually more conservative and staged than for other pigmentation.

factors.title: Cumulative exposure
factors.text: Melasma usually reflects cumulative exposure and skin behaviour over years, not a single recent cause.

factors.title: Barrier and turnover
factors.text: Changes to the skin barrier and cell turnover rate influence how visible melasma becomes over time.

factors.title: Individual variation
factors.text: How melasma presents and responds to treatment varies meaningfully between skin types.

recommendedText: Considered as a first-line, course-based approach to melasma, given its lower risk of aggravating pigment compared to heat-based devices.
alongsideText: Often assessed alongside, since these concerns frequently share the same treatment options.

steps.title: Assessment first
steps.text: We confirm melasma rather than assume it, since it is often confused with other pigmentation and responds poorly to the wrong treatment.

steps.title: Conservative, staged treatment
steps.text: Lower-heat, course-based options are used first, with intensity increased only if needed and tolerated.

steps.title: Strict sun protection throughout
steps.text: Daily broad-spectrum SPF is non-negotiable during treatment, since UV exposure can undo progress quickly.

steps.title: Ongoing monitoring
steps.text: Melasma can recur, so we review and adjust the plan over time rather than treating it as a one-off.
